Claim 1 (Currently Amended): A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time-integrated irradiance of at least 5 hours of solar illumination; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, the annealing in response to the illuminating of the photovoltaic cell.

Claim 2 (Currently Amended): The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and one of: wherein the photovoltaic cell receives a time-integrated irradiance of at least 20 hours of solar illumination; wherein the photovoltaic cell receives a time-integrated irradiance of at least 16 hours of solar illumination while being heated to at least 50 degrees Celsius; and wherein the photovoltaic cell is irradiated using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, and wherein the solar concentrator increases the irradiance on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5.

Claim 3 (Currently Amended): The method of Claim 2, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein annealing of the photovoltaic cell further comprises illuminating the photovoltaic cell.

Claim 4 (Currently Amended): The method of Claim 3, wherein illuminating the photovoltaic cell during the annealing is performed such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time-integrated irradiance of at least 10 minutes of solar illumination.

Claim 10 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates sunlight.
